prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of commitments and policies

- Economy and tax: Eliminate the deficit, then run a surplus under a new fiscal rule; no increases in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000; crack down on tax evasion/avoidance; complete bank ring‑fencing, strengthen bonus clawback, maintain the bank levy; promote challenger banks and fintech; lead on international tax transparency.

- Regional growth and infrastructure: Devolution of economic, transport and social care powers to cities with elected mayors; major investment in the North and Midlands; over £100bn capital plan including HS2/HS3, electrification, Crossrail, road upgrades, cycling; freeze regulated rail fares in real terms; superfast broadband to 95% by end‑2017, push to ultrafast; improve mobile coverage and 5G leadership.

- Jobs, skills and business: Aim for full employment and 2 million more jobs; 3 million new apprenticeships; tougher work requirements for 18–21s, time‑limited Youth Allowance; cut £10bn of red tape; treble Start Up Loans; permanent Office of Tax Simplification; small business late‑payment conciliation; publish gender pay gaps at large firms; halve the disability employment gap; support science with £6.9bn capital, Catapults, and industrial strategies.

- Welfare and families: “Tax‑Free Minimum Wage” law linking the Personal Allowance to the Minimum Wage; reduce the household benefit cap to £23,000; two‑year freeze of most working‑age benefits (with exemptions); roll out Universal Credit; tax‑free childcare up to £2,000 per child and 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3–4‑year‑olds.

- Immigration: Target lower net migration; restrict access to in‑work benefits and social housing for recent EU arrivals; require EU jobseekers to leave after six months if not employed; strengthen deportation and removals; landlord checks; tougher enforcement against illegal working; Controlling Migration Fund; English fluency requirement for public‑facing roles.

- Education: Protect per‑pupil funding; higher primary standards with resits if needed; promote EBacc subjects; turn failing/coasting schools into academies; open at least 500 new free schools; continue pupil premium; recruit more maths/physics teachers; expand UTCs and degree apprenticeships; uncap university places; introduce postgraduate loans; create a teaching excellence framework.

- NHS and care: Increase funding in real terms with at least £8bn extra by 2020; 7‑day GP access and hospital services; named GP and online services; cancer strategy and continued Cancer Drugs Fund; expand mental health access and standards; dementia strategy and more support for carers; integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs and allow deferred payments; patient access to electronic records with opt‑out.

- Housing and communities: Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under‑40 first‑time buyers); extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; extend Help to Buy and launch a Help to Buy ISA; deliver 275,000 additional affordable homes and 10,000 below‑market‑rent homes; focus on brownfield, protect the Green Belt; support locally led garden towns.

- Environment and energy: Plant 11m trees; protect forests; create a UK/Overseas Territories “Blue Belt” of marine sites; improve air, water and flood defences; tackle illegal wildlife trade; promote competition and smart meters by 2020; insulate 1m more homes; support nuclear, offshore wind, CCS and new technologies; end new public subsidy for onshore wind and give local communities the final say; support shale gas with community benefits; meet climate goals cost‑effectively.

- Crime, justice and security: Continue police reform, technology adoption and cyber capability; overhaul complaints; crime prevention on legal highs and alcohol; modernise prisons and tackle contraband; Victims’ Law; strengthen action on violence against women and girls, FGM and forced marriage; update communications data powers with oversight; replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights; counter‑extremism orders and measures against online radicalisation.

- Older people and pensions: Maintain the triple lock; introduce the single‑tier state pension; retain pensioner benefits (with a “temperature test” for Winter Fuel Payment abroad); pension freedoms and reduced inheritance tax on pension pots; raise the effective inheritance tax threshold for a family home to £1m, funded by reduced pension tax relief for highest earners.

- Constitution, Europe, defence and foreign policy: Devolution to Scotland and Wales; implement English votes for English laws; boundary review and electoral integrity measures; hold an in‑out EU referendum by end‑2017 after renegotiation; protect the Single Market and the pound; maintain armed forces (army not below 82,000), renew the nuclear deterrent, invest in equipment and cyber; keep aid at 0.7% GNI focused on health, education, WASH, gender equality and crisis response.
